t: #2595 — Number of Even and Odd Bits
o: Given n ≤ 1000, look at its binary representation indexed from the right (least significant bit = index 0). Count the 1-bits at even indices and at odd indices, returning [even, odd]. For n = 50 (110010₂) the set bits sit at indices 1, 4, 5, giving [1, 2]. For n = 2 (10₂) the only set bit is at index 1, giving [0, 1]. Constraints are tiny, so a simple bit loop suffices.
k: Bit i of n is (n >> i) & 1.
Only about 10 bits need checking for n ≤ 1000.

a.i: Walk bit positions i = 0, 1, 2, … while n has bits left; test (n >> i) & 1 and add to the even or odd bucket depending on the parity of i.
s: For each bit index i, extract the bit and add it to even if i is even, else odd.
a.t: O(log n) — one iteration per bit of n.

w: Trivial warm-up. An alternative one-liner style masks with 0x55555555 (even positions) and 0xAAAAAAAA (odd positions) and uses popcount. Watch for off-by-one confusion: index 0 is the least significant bit and is even.
